CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Beverly is a 24-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presenting for her yearly examination. She reports that she has been doing well overall. She began working in a bakery this summer and has been enjoying the job. However, she notes that due to her proximity to many desserts at work, she has been snacking frequently and consuming significantly more desserts than usual. She reports that her blood sugars have been up and down, which she attributes to her diet. She confirms she has been taking her medications as prescribed and has not missed any doses. She acknowledges that resisting the temptation of the bakery treats has been challenging. Her blood pressure has been good despite the fluctuations in her diabetes levels. She reports sleeping well, getting a full eight hours of sleep nightly. She denies any concerning symptoms or thoughts of self-harm.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Otherwise negative per nurse review. No additional concerns reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension
Grade 2 systolic ejection fraction back ejection murmur (known, unchanged)

MEDICATIONS
Metformin 500 mg twice daily
Lisinopril 10 mg once daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recently started working at a bakery this summer. Works in close proximity to desserts and baked goods.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Alert and oriented
Neurological: Grip strength equal bilaterally. Sensation intact to light touch in extremities. Motor strength intact.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. Grade 2 systolic ejection fraction back ejection murmur noted, unchanged from prior. No carotid bruits. Good pulses.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Neck: No thyromegaly.
Extremities: No edema.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1c: Elevated
Blood pressure: Normal, well-controlled
Vital signs: Stable

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Currently suboptimally controlled. Hemoglobin A1c elevated, target is less than 7%, preferably less than 6%. Continue current metformin 500 mg twice daily. No medication changes at this time as hyperglycemia appears diet-related. Patient to reduce snacking and dessert consumption. Patient to check fasting blood glucose in the morning and call in results in approximately 2 weeks. Follow-up in 2 months to reassess glycemic control. If no improvement, will consider adding additional antidiabetic medication.

2. Hypertension - Stable and well-controlled. Continue lisinopril 10 mg once daily. No changes to current regimen.
